requirements.statement: Every non-trivial repository task starts with the Claude+Codex orchestrator when both seats are available.

markers: Every non-trivial repository task **must begin with**
Use the duo for every non-trivial repository task.

requirements.statement: Claude and Codex independently research, analyze risks, and draft complete plans from the same immutable brief before either sees the other conclusion.

markers: draft a plan in parallel before seeing the other's conclusions
an implementation plan and test strategy

requirements.statement: Claude compares two or three designs unless the brief fixes one direction; Codex challenges feasibility, failure modes, security, testing, and maintainability.

markers: brief already fixes a clear direction
failure modes, security, testing, and maintainability

requirements.statement: Both seats approve the exact plan and task version; any change invalidates both approvals.

markers: A changed plan invalidates both approvals

requirements.statement: Codex implements and first-verifies the approved work regardless of the host harness.

The directly invoked primary Fable seat independently reviews the settled design and integrated code for correctness, proportionality, maintainability, security, and evidence, and owns the final quality verdict; a fallback is recorded without claiming Fable review.

markers: owns the final code and design quality verdict
never report that Fable reviewed the work

requirements.statement: The directly invoked Fable-class seat owns Claude judgment; it may route deterministic UI/MCP collection to Opus medium and ambiguous multi-step tool operation to Opus high, but workers never settle the judgment.
Peer work uses native interactive vendor sessions with configured tools and MCPs, never headless model execution.
A missing peer degrades only after proven unavailability and is recorded; a mid-run loss retries boundedly and blocks rather than silently continuing.

Cross-model callers invoke the Fable and Codex primary seats directly at high by default, escalate to xhigh only on defined demand or failure triggers, and never transfer primary ownership to internal workers.

markers: directly at high effort by default
Escalate the primary Fable seat to xhigh
the primary Codex seat still owns implementation and first verification
never let an internal worker replace either duo seat

requirements.statement: Where line coverage is supported, aggregate production coverage has a hard 80 percent floor and a normal 90 percent target; a weaker repository setting cannot undercut it.
Verification covers relevant unit, integration, end-to-end, security, and rendered UI behavior; unavailable or not applicable are never reported as passes.

markers: Tool unavailability is a blocker or declared limitation, not a pass

requirements.statement: Design and implementation use the smallest coherent durable solution for the accepted lifecycle, scale, change rate, contributor and integration breadth, operational risk, and reversibility; reject both speculative complexity and brittle under-design; preserve justified modularity and reuse; handle accepted edge and failure cases; clarify materially missing context; and treat project size or raw line count only as inputs, never automatic architecture rules.

markers: Write only what earns its keep

requirements.statement: UI work reuses an existing design system when present and composes recurring tokens, accessible primitives, application components, and explicit state into views without duplicated one-off implementations or speculative framework layers.

markers: no new design system or higher-order abstraction for a one-off surface

requirements.statement: Security review unions a Claude defender and Codex attacker lens, preserves divergence, and blocks loss of a required second vendor.
Evidence outranks agreement and fabricated or unverifiable claims are defects.

markers: Unverifiable or fabricated claims are defects

requirements.statement: Missing product intent, public contracts, security boundaries, or irreversible choices block for clarification; local reversible details follow repository evidence without inventing requirements.

markers: Ambiguous input is a blocker: ask, never assume
Treat an unclear requirement, API, or fact as a stop-and-verify

requirements.statement: Destructive protected-branch actions, guard bypasses, and raw secret handling remain prohibited while public research and brokered tools stay available.

markers: public network and live search are enabled

requirements.statement: Parallel work is bounded by host resources, has one owner/branch/worktree per task, serializes shared contracts and integration, and verifies the combined diff.
Work consults product scope and capabilities before building and uses architecture, ADRs, and recall for rationale rather than inventing it.
Outputs are audience-shaped, evidence-backed, explicit about limitations and N/A, and preserve material disagreement.

markers: never cut key information to condense
records both outputs without collapsing disagreements

requirements.statement: Substantial prose is reviewed in its full project, audience, medium, and task context; preserves technical meaning and credible documented voice; removes unsupported certainty, sycophancy, inflation, and obstructive formatting without fabricating personality or applying lexical, punctuation, list, or emoji blacklists.

markers: There is no universal word, punctuation, formatting, or emoji blacklist
Do not use an AI detector

requirements.statement: Agents prepare reviewable PRs and evidence but a human merges protected branches.
Token efficiency is evaluated as reliable contract adherence per loaded token and never authorizes removal or weakening of a semantic duty.

markers: Token consciousness means reliable adherence per loaded token
